Procedures for Calculating SGPs
Damian Betebenner & Adam VanIwaarden
Center for Assessment

June 13th, 2024

Overview & Setup
• The methodology and software used to calculate student growth percentiles is
 open source.
 • Paper documenting the methodology: Norm- and Criterion-Referenced
 Student Growth (2008)
 • Calculation of SGPs utilize (the latest versions of) the R software
 environment in conjunction with the SGP package that was created and
 currently maintained by Dr. Damian Betebenner and Adam VanIwaarden.
 • All R source code associated with MA DESE analyses is located on GitHub (no
 PII information)
 • MCAS: https://github.com/CenterForAssessment/Massachusetts
 • WIDA-ACCESS: https://github.com/CenterForAssessment/WIDA_MA

Outline for Calculations
• Calculation of SGPs have always followed the principle that data
 cleaning is 90% of the work.
 • Step 1: Data preparation: Take raw data files provided by DESE
 and create a long formatted .Rdata file suitable for SGP
 analyses.
 • Step 2: SGP Analysis: Take long formatted .Rdata file from Step
 1 and utilize SGP package for analysis.
 • Step 3: Post-Processing: Produces state specific formats for the
 output

Step 1: Data Preparation
• Source code for data preparation is located (as is all source code) on Github.
• The nomenclature for the names of the source code files is, for example,
 Massachusetts_Data_LONG_2024.R to denote the data preparation file for
 2024 data.
• Data preparation involves getting naming conventions for variables to align
 with the SGP package, making sure variable mode is aligned with SGP
 calculations, making sure variable levels are consistent with previous years,
 identifying duplicate cases and resolving them.
• For WIDA data preparation, create ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL (WIDA Level 1,
 WIDA Level 2, …) and ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL_ORIGINAL (1.0, 1.1, …, 2.0, 2.1,
 …)

Step 2: Data Analysis - MCAS
• Source code for data analysis is located (as is all source code)
 on Github.
• The nomenclature for the names of the source code files is,
 for example, Massachusetts_SGP_2024.R to denote the data
 analysis file for 2024 data.
• SGP source code specifies the types of norm- and criterion-
 referenced SGP analyses to conduct.

Step 2: Data Analysis - MCAS
• Some odds and ends of MCAS SGP analyses:
 • Due to historical decisions to take advantage of granularity of theta
 scores, MCAS SGP analyses currently utilize student theta values
 instead of scaled scores.
 • Projections and lagged projections are calculated originally in SGP
 terms (based upon a 5 year time frame to reach/maintain the
 desired level of achievement). Those targets are converted to scale
 score targets and utilized by DESE.
 • Current targets are calculated and “banked” to be used the
 following year (versus using on-time/current norms)

Step 2: Data Analysis - WIDA-ACCESS
• Some odds and ends of WIDA-ACCESS SGP analyses:
 • SGP analyses utilize the composite scaled score
 • Projections and lagged projections are calculated originally in SGP terms (based
 upon a variable year time frame to reach English language proficiency/4.2 level on
 WIDA-ACCESS). Those are converted to scale score targets and utilized by DESE.
 • Scale score targets are calculated for 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 year time frames. Based
 upon time in MA receiving ELL services, a time-frame is specified.
 • Scale-scores are converted back to WIDA-ACCESS achievement levels (1.0, 1.1, 1.2,
 …, 2.0, 2.1, …) This conversion is done in a post-processing phase using R source
 code provided by https://github.com/CenterForAssessment/WIDA_MA/blob/
 master/WIDA_MA_Formatted_Output_2023.R
